 1.
The present matter was taken up for hearing on 19.09.2024 and the following order was passed:

"4. Learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner at the outset submitted that the informant has married the petitioner and they are staying together as husband and wife and leading a happy conjugal married life.
On perusal of the case diary as well the 164 statement of the victim it appears that same was recorded prior to the marriage as alleged by the counsel for the petitioner.
Although, the victim was present before this Court through the virtual mode however, due to network issues she could not be heard in the matter.
In the aforesaid factual background, this court directs that the 164 statement of the victim to be recorded again.

Accordingly, learned counsel for the victim is requested to inform the victim to remain present before the Chandan Sahu vs State Of Odisha & Another .... Opp. ... on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45415315/
1 I.O. for recording of her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
5.

sentences.text: Further, learned counsel for the State is directed to intimate the concerned Inspector-in-Charge, of the Police Station, who in turn will inform the informant/victim that the present case will be taken up for final hearing 23.10.2024 and if the informant/victim has any objection, he/she shall appear through virtual mode on the said date, if the informant/victim agrees to appear through virtual mode.
In such eventuality, the concerned Inspector-in-Charge shall make necessary arrangement for the appearance of the informant/victim on the said date."
2. Pursuant to the said order, on 01.10.2024, the statement of the victim girl has been recorded under Section 164 of the Cr. P.C. for the second time.

She in her statement has inter alia, stated as under:
"I and Chandan Sahu were in love.
We were staying in the Garden Plaza Hotel at Puri and we had physical relationship.
But since I belong to the S.C. category and my husband Chandan Sahu belongs to O.B.C. category, the family members of my husband were not agreed for our marriage.
Despite lots of efforts, they could not understand, for which I instituted this case.
Then the family members agreed and they solemnized our marriage.
Now we are living happily.
I am happy with Chandan Sahu and I want to close this case.
I do hereby certify that, I have recorded the statement of victim u/s 164 Cr. P.C. in her exact verbatim in Odia.
I read over and explained the contents to her in Odia to which she admitted to be to be true and correct and put her signature in two separate sheets in my presence."
3. The petitioner and the opposite party No.2 are present in the Court today through the Video Conferencing mode.
They are being represented by their respective counsel and identified by them.

They have also filed the photocopies of their self-attested Aadhaar Cards to establish their identity,
which are taken on record.
4.

At the instance of the opposite party No.2, the F.I.R. in connection with Sea Beach P.S. Case No.137 of 2019 corresponding to G.R. Case No.22 of 2021 came to be registered against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 493/417/376(2)(n) of the IPC pending in the Court of the learned Special Judge, Puri.

entities.text: Sea Beach P.S. Case No.137 of 2019
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 5. The investigation in the present case is still going on.
At this stage, the parties have settled their dispute and the petitioner has married with the opposite party No.2 and they are leading happy conjugal life.
On the basis of the settlement, the petitioner has filed the present case for quashing.

6. The opposite party No.2 has also filed an affidavit before this Court on 16.08.2024, inter alia,
stating as under:
Chandan Sahu vs State Of Odisha & Another .... Opp. ... on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45415315/
2 "3.

sentences.text: That, in due course of their relationship the deponent and the petitioner visited different places and established physical relationship with consent but since the mother of the petitioner did not agree for the solemnization of marriage, the deponent lodged a written report before the IIC, Sea Beach Police Station for which Sea Beach P.S. Case No. 137 dated 12/09/2019 was registered against the petitioner for commission of alleged offences u/s. 493/417/376(2)(n) of IPC and to the knowledge of the deponent the case is under investigation.

4. That, during course of investigation the petitioner was arrested on 07.10.2019 and during hearing of the bail application the deponent also appeared and submitted that she had married to the petitioner and their social marriage would be taken place at later stage and further submitted that she was not interested to proceed against the petitioner as the matter has been amicably settled in the presence of family members of the both the parties.
5. That, the deponent humbly submits that she had already married to the petitioner and residing in the house of the petitioner as his wife.
6. That, in view of the above development the deponent is not interested to proceed with the case and if the case will be continued it will affect her marital life."

7. On the changing circumstances, the opposite party No.2 is joining with the petitioner by praying before this Court for quashing of the entire criminal prosecution initiated by her against the petitioner.
8. Mrs. Nayak, learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State submits that, essentially the dispute is inter se parties.
They have settled their dispute.

Since the petitioner and the opposite party No.2 are leading happy conjugal life, there is no legal impediment in quashing the F.I.R.
9.

Regard being had to the circumstances mentioned above and in view of the Judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and another reported in 2012 (10) SCC 303 and B.S. Joshi & others v. State of Haryana & another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675 and MadhavraoJi Wajirao Scindia & another v. Sambhajirao ChandrojiraoAngre and others,
reported in AIR 1988 SC 709, subjecting the petitioner to the rigors of the trial would be a futile exercise.

10. Taking into consideration the aforementioned judgments, the facts of the case and submission made at bar, the F.I.R. in Sea Beach P.S. Case No.137 of 2019 corresponding to G.R. Case No.22 of 2021 pending in the Court of learned Special Judge, Puri and the consequential proceedings arising therefrom qua the petitioner is quashed.
